files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.AcknowledgementCommandException

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.AmqpSecurityException
files.Summary: Represents a security-related failure that occurs while using the AMQP client. This exception is thrown when an operation is denied due to authentication, authorization, or other security checks performed by the broker or client.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.Client
files.Summary: Represents a reusable AMQP client that manages an underlying connection and provides access to message broker producers, consumers and subscribers. The client is safe for concurrent use and supports asynchronous startup and disposal.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.ClientOptions
files.Summary: Represents the configuration options for the NMS AMQP client, including connection string and redelivery policy.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.ConnectionException
files.Summary: Represents a failure to establish or maintain a connection with the AMQP broker. This exception is thrown when the client is unable to connect, loses an existing connection, or encounters errors related to the underlying transport.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.ConsumerExtensions
files.Summary: Runtime helpers for extracting capability-specific interfaces from a generic instance. These helpers avoid breaking changes while providing explicit runtime checks for acknowledgement/transactional features.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.ConsumerOptions
files.Summary: Options for configuring a message consumer of a queue.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.DefaultRedeliveryPolicy
files.Summary: Represents the default redelivery policy used to determine message redelivery behavior.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.DestinationType
files.Summary: Represents the type of the destination such as a queue or topic.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.ErrorHandlerAsync
files.Summary: Delegate invoked when an error occurs while processing messages.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.IAcknowledgeConsumer
files.Summary: Represents a consumer that supports explicit acknowledge and negative acknowledge operations (e.g. ClientAcknowledge or IndividualAcknowledge modes).

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.IBytesMessage
files.Summary:
A BytesMessage object is used to send a message containing a stream of uninterpreted bytes. It inherits from the Message interface and adds a bytes message body. The receiver of the message supplies the interpretation of the bytes.

This message type is for client encoding of existing message formats. If possible, one of the other self-defining message types should be used instead.

Although the NMS API allows the use of message properties with byte messages, they are typically not used, since the inclusion of properties may affect the format.

When the message is first created, and when ClearBody is called, the body of the message is in write-only mode. After the first call to Reset has been made, the message body is in read-only mode. After a message has been sent, the client that sent it can retain and modify it without affecting the message that has been sent. The same message object can be sent multiple times. When a message has been received, the provider has called Reset so that the message body is in read-only mode for the client.

If ClearBody is called on a message in read-only mode, the message body is cleared and the message is in write-only mode.

If a client attempts to read a message in write-only mode, a MessageNotReadableException is thrown.

If a client attempts to write a message in read-only mode, a MessageNotWriteableException is thrown.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.IClient
files.Summary: Represents a client that manages AMQP connection lifecycle and related producer/consumer/subscriber managers.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.IConsumer
files.Summary: Represents a message consumer that can receive messages from a destination (queue or topic) in a messaging system.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.IConsumerManager
files.Summary: Manager abstraction responsible for creating and managing instances. Implementations provide asynchronous creation methods with various configuration options and support deletion/lifecycle management of created consumers.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.IDestination
files.Summary: A base interface for destinations such as queues or topics

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.IDestinationProvider
files.Summary: Provides methods for creating temporary destinations and resolving named destinations (queues and topics) in a messaging system.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.IMapMessage
files.Summary: Represents a Map message which contains key and value pairs which are of primitive types

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.IMessage
files.Summary: Represents a message either to be sent to a message broker or received from a message broker.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.IMessageCreator
files.Summary: Defines a contract for creating various types of messages in a messaging system. Implementations of this interface are responsible for providing methods to create different message types, such as bytes, map, object, stream, and text messages, both with and without initial content. All methods are asynchronous and return tasks that complete with the created message instances.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.IMessageProducer
files.Summary: Represents a message producer that can create messages and destinations.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.IPrimitiveMap
files.Summary: Represents a Map of primitive types where the keys are all string instances and the values are strings or numbers.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.IProducer
files.Summary: Defines the contract for a message producer that creates and sends messages to queues or topics in a messaging system. Provides asynchronous methods for message creation, sending, and transaction management. Implementations are expected to be safe for concurrent use and to honor cancellation semantics where applicable.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.IProducerManager
files.Summary: Factory abstraction responsible for creating and managing instances. Implementations create producers for destinations or queues and support deletion and lifecycle observation. All creation methods are asynchronous to allow for remote or I/O-bound producer initialization.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.IQueue
files.Summary: Represents a queue in a message broker.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.IRedeliveryPolicy
files.Summary: Represents the redelivery policy used by the AMQP client for supporting message brokers.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.IStreamMessage
files.Summary:
A StreamMessage object is used to send a stream of primitive types in the .NET programming language. It is filled and read sequentially. It inherits from the Message interface and adds a stream message body.

The primitive types can be read or written explicitly using methods for each type. They may also be read or written generically as objects. For instance, a call to IStreamMessage.WriteInt32(6) is equivalent to StreamMessage.WriteObject( (Int32)6 ). Both forms are provided, because the explicit form is convenient for static programming, and the object form is needed when types are not known at compile time.

When the message is first created, and when ClearBody is called, the body of the message is in write-only mode. After the first call to reset has been made, the message body is in read-only mode. After a message has been sent, the client that sent it can retain and modify it without affecting the message that has been sent. The same message object can be sent multiple times. When a message has been received, the provider has called reset so that the message body is in read-only mode for the client.

If ClearBody is called on a message in read-only mode, the message body is cleared and the message body is in write-only mode.

If a client attempts to read a message in write-only mode, a MessageNotReadableException is thrown.

If a client attempts to write a message in read-only mode, a MessageNotWriteableException is thrown.

IStreamMessage objects support the following conversion table. The marked cases must be supported. The unmarked cases must throw a NMSException. The String-to-primitive conversions may throw a runtime exception if the primitive's valueOf() method does not accept it as a valid String representation of the primitive.

A value written as the row type can be read as the column type.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.ISubscriber
files.Summary: Represents a message consumer that can receive messages from a destination (queue or topic) in a messaging system.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.ISubscriberManager
files.Summary: Manager abstraction responsible for creating and managing instances. Implementations provide asynchronous creation methods with various configuration options and support deletion/lifecycle management of created subscribers.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.ITemporaryQueue
files.Summary: Represents a temporary queue which exists for the duration of the IConnection which created it.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.ITemporaryTopic
files.Summary: Represents a temporary topic which exists for the duration of the IConnection which created it.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.ITextMessage
files.Summary: Represents a text based message

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.ITopic
files.Summary: Represents a topic in a message broker.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.ITransactionalConsumer
files.Summary: Represents a consumer that supports transactional commands (Commit/Rollback).

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.IllegalStateException
files.Summary: Thrown when an operation is requested that is invalid given the current state of the object or client. Use this exception to indicate that the requested action cannot be performed until the object reaches an appropriate state (for example, calling an API method when the connection is closed).

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.InvalidClientIDException
files.Summary: Thrown when the client identifier provided for a connection is invalid. This mirrors the behavior of the Apache NMS InvalidClientIDException and is raised when a client id is malformed, already in use, or otherwise not acceptable to the broker or client implementation.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.InvalidDestinationException
files.Summary: Thrown when an operation references a destination that is invalid for the requested action. Examples include non-existent destinations, destinations of the wrong type, or destinations with malformed names.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.InvalidSelectorException
files.Summary: Thrown when a message selector is invalid or cannot be parsed/evaluated by the client or broker. This exception indicates that the selector expression is malformed or uses unsupported features.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.MessageAction
files.Summary: Defines the actions that can be taken for a message processed by the consumer.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.MessageEOFException
files.Summary: Thrown when an unexpected end-of-file or end-of-stream is encountered while reading a message. This indicates that the message payload or wire-format ended prematurely and the client could not fully deserialize the message.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.MessageFormatException
files.Summary: Thrown when a message cannot be parsed or decoded because its format is invalid or unsupported. This indicates that the wire-format or payload does not conform to the expected message schema and the client cannot construct a valid message object from the received data.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.MessageNotReadableException
files.Summary: Thrown when an attempt is made to read data from a message that is not readable. This commonly occurs when a message is in a write-only state or when the message payload cannot be accessed for reading.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.MessageNotWriteableException
files.Summary: Thrown when an attempt is made to write to a message that is not writable. This occurs for messages that are in a read-only state or when the message content cannot be modified (for example after the message has been sent).

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.MessageProcessorAsync
files.Summary: Delegate invoked when a message is received from the message queue.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.MessageQueueEventArgs
files.Summary: Provides data for events raised when a message is queued, processed or otherwise observed by the consumer pipeline.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.MessageTransformerAsync
files.Summary: A delegate that a client can register that will be called to preprocess messages allowing the client to modify message properties and/or transform a message from one type to another, StreamMessage to TextMessage, ObjectMessage to TextMessage containing XML, etc. Return null or original message if no change.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.MsgDeliveryMode
files.Summary: Define an enumerated array of message delivery modes. Provider-specific values can be used to extend this enumerated mode. TIBCO is known to provide a third value of ReliableDelivery. At minimum, a provider must support Persistent and NonPersistent.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.MsgPriority
files.Summary: Define an enumerated array of message priorities.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.ProducerOptions
files.Summary: Options used to configure a message producer.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.RedeliveryPolicy
files.Summary: A policy used to customize exactly how you want the redelivery to work.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.ResourceAllocationException
files.Summary: Represents a failure that occurs when required resources cannot be allocated.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.ResponderOptions
files.Summary: Configuration options that control where and how a responder sends reply messages. These options allow specifying an explicit , or alternatively a destination name and type to be used when creating the response destination.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.ResponseDestinationType
files.Summary: Specifies the type of destination to which a response message is sent.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.SendResponseException
files.Summary: Represents an exception that is thrown when an error occurs while sending a response message.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.ServiceCollectionExtensions
files.Summary: Provides extension methods for to register NMS AMQP client services.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.StartupException
files.Summary: Represents an exception that is thrown when an error occurs while starting up a Message Receiver or a Producer.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.SubscriberOptions
files.Summary: Options used to configure a subscriber to a topic.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.TransactionInProgressException
files.Summary: Thrown when an operation cannot be performed because a transaction is already in progress on the connection or session. Use this exception to indicate conflicting transaction operations such as attempting to begin a new transaction while another is active, or to mark that certain actions are illegal during a transaction lifecycle.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.TransactionRolledBackException
files.Summary: Thrown when a transaction has been rolled back instead of committed. This exception indicates that the work performed within the transaction was not applied, either due to an explicit rollback request, an error during the transaction, or a broker-initiated rollback.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.TransactionalCommandException
files.Summary: Represents an exception that is thrown when a transactional command fails during execution.

files.Title: CodersRealm.AmqpClient.UserHandlerException
files.Summary: Represents an exception that is thrown when a user-provided handler throws an exception.
